The complete real-parameter covariance spectrum follows from the three displayed one-variable beta-polynomial integrals, plus vanishing mixed moments by reflection and conditional symmetry. All three rational eigenvalue differences are factored and signed, proving \(\lambda_B\) largest for \(t>1\) and the single least-eigenspace switch at \(t=3/2\). The volume derivative and the constant-face-type assertion have independent elementary proofs. The supplied actual path artifacts/verify.py reproduced 15 profiles (118 vertices, 176 tetrahedra) using exact rational moments and checked all symbolic identities; finite tests support, rather than replace, the all-real proof.

originality.rationale: The published 2021 four-cube critical-section paper supplies the exact volume-critical normal \((1,1,2,2)\), not the covariance of the uniform-volume distribution in its sections. The 2023 cube-section paper also treats normal-direction volume Hessians, which are not the within-section inertia tensor. The 2023 general moments paper implies that such moments are algorithmically computable, but does not give the evaluated three-eigenvalue spectrum or exact least-eigenspace transition at \(t=3/2\); the equal-weight hypersimplex identification only handles the \(t=1\) endpoint. Multiple specific semantic searches and previous-claim comparisons found no implication that supplies the exact new result. Historical priority remains provisional; generic integration could facilitate an independent derivation, not automatically establish this particular evaluated identity.

value.rationale: This is the exact classification of a natural intrinsic second-moment invariant of the one-parameter family of central four-cube slices containing the previously discovered non-diagonal volume-critical normal \((1,1,2,2)\). It identifies a sharp least-variance axis exchange at \(t=3/2\) inside a constant face-lattice chamber, distinct from scalar-volume stationarity at \(t=2\), and completely determines the three eigenvalue functions and condition number. That separation between intrinsic inertia and section volume is a structural mathematical fact, not a pre-existing scalar volume formula or an arbitrary finite sample. The narrow family is justified by its role in known critical-section geometry.
